title: Web Dev Tutorial
objective: Steer AI toward an intended design by writing specific prompts and refining them based on what comes back. Judge AI output against your own intent, and decide when to accept, redirect, or override it. Use the vocabulary of web design (hero, feature cards, interactive canvas, call-to-action) to analyze what makes a page effective and to describe what you want built. Describe a problem with enough context for AI to give a useful explanation and fix. Verify an AI-proposed fix before trusting it, confirming the problem is resolved and nothing new broke.

project.description: Your final project for the Web Dev Tutorial.

build.title: Build with AI
build.description: Students move from asking for something, to specifying it, to judging what comes back.

language.title: Language of web dev
language.description: Students move from spotting the blocks, to explaining them, to using the vocabulary themselves.

debug.title: Debug with AI

checkpoints.title: Introduction
checkpoints.description: An introduction to the Web Dev Tutorial.

panels.text: Click continue after your class watches the introduction video.

###Start with a vision. 
Who needs something, and what would you make for them? You’ll pick up the language of web developers as you build with AI.

###Spark your ideas.
Check out these examples then think about what YOU want to build!

###Second Helpings
Connect extra food with the people who need it, before it goes to waste.

####Open Door
Make it easier for a teen to find the right support at the right moment.

###Puente
Make sure every family can understand what’s happening at school.

####Build it!
In this lesson, your path is unique. Share your idea and your coding experience, and your lesson shifts with every answer along the way.

steps.title: Write your first prompt.
steps.instructions: **Write your first prompt.** Tell the AI what you want to build. What you write shapes where your path begins.

questions.questionTitle: Which sentence sounds most like you?

choices.text: I’m new to this. I haven’t worked with website code before.
I know some of the basics, like headings, buttons, and links that make up a page.
I can describe how a page looks, like its colors, fonts, and layout.
I can describe how a page behaves, like what happens when someone clicks or types.

questions.questionTitle: You want a button that changes color when someone clicks it. Which instruction would work best?

choices.text: Style the button with a blue background color.
Add a click event that changes the button’s color.
Make the button look better and work better.
Add a button element that says “Click me.”

questions.questionTitle: You want a page with a heading and three cards in a row. Which instruction would work best?

choices.text: Add a heading and three cards.
Add an h1 and three div elements.
Add an h1, then place three cards side by side.
Use flexbox to lay out three card divs in a row.

checkpoints.title: Add Details
checkpoints.description: Add concrete details (layout, colors, content, purpose) so the prompt isn't vague

steps.title: Practice - Web Lab Practice
steps.instructions:
Someone named Sam wrote this prompt for a panda fan page:

*“Make a website about pandas.”*

Look at the preview to see what it built. Sam is not happy with it.

*Then:*

Pick one thing you’d change. Then write a better prompt for Sam. Name the part you’re changing and add at least two details, like a color, a tone, or something pandas do.

steps.title: Apply to project
steps.instructions:
Now it’s your turn. Look at your own page and pick one thing you want to change.

**Do This:**

1.  Write a detailed prompt that names the part of your page you want to change.  *Think color, size, wording, or tone. Change your heading, text, background or buttons.*
1.  Look at the preview to see what changed. If it’s not what you meant, say what to change next.
steps.instructionsPrompt: Have the student look at their own page, pick one thing to change, and write a detailed prompt that names that part of the page and uses 2+ specific design details, such as color, size, wording, or tone. Name the actual element or text on their page that the change builds on.

checkpoints.title: Tweak It
checkpoints.description: Respond to what came back with a follow-up that targets one thing that's off

panels.text:
###Tweak it
Pick the one thing you want to improve and say exactly what to change.

**Weak Prompt:** “Make it better.”

--> What’s “it”? What’s “better”?

**Strong Prompt:** “The paragraph sounds like an encyclopedia. Make it sound like a hungry panda. Keep the heading.”

--> Names the problem, the fix, and what to keep.

steps.title: Apply to project
steps.instructions: Pick the one thing you want to improve. Write a follow-up prompt that names that part, says what to change, and says what to keep.
steps.instructionsPrompt: Have the student pick the one thing on their page they want to improve and write a follow-up prompt that names that part, says what to change, and says what to keep, as in: The [part] is [problem]. Change it so [detail]. Keep the [part you like]. Name a specific element the AI already built.

checkpoints.title: Edit by Hand
checkpoints.description: Decide when a direct edit beats another prompt, and make it

steps.title: Edit by Hand
steps.instructions:
Sam’s page is almost done, but three small things are off.

1.  Look at the preview and find what’s wrong: a typo in the heading, a heading that’s the wrong color, and a button with the wrong words.
2.  Fix each one yourself in the code. Don’t ask the AI.
3.  Check the preview again to see your fixes.
4.  Write one sentence: why was editing faster than writing another prompt?

panels.text:
###Edit by Hand
Sometimes the fastest fix is your own hands.

- Edit it yourself when the change is tiny: a word, a color, a typo.
- Prompt again when the change is bigger or you’re not sure how.

Accept it if it matches, and fix what doesn’t.

questions.questionTitle: Sam asked the AI: “Make a panda page with a green background, the heading ‘Panda Fan Club,’ a paragraph that sounds like a hungry panda, and a button that says ‘Meet the pandas.’” The AI built the green background and the heading correctly. But the paragraph still sounds like an encyclopedia, and the button says “Meet the panda.” What should Sam do next?

choices.text: Accept it, since the background and heading are right
Start over with a detailed new prompt
Write a follow-up prompt to fix the paragraph, and fix the button typo in the code
Fix both in the code by hand

steps.title: Project
steps.instructions:
1.  Find one small thing on your page to fix, like a word, or a color.
2.  Change it yourself in the code.
3.  Look at the preview to check your fix.

Was editing faster than asking the AI?
steps.instructionsPrompt: Have the student find one small thing on their page to fix, like a word or a color, change it themselves in the code, and look at the preview to check the fix. Name the actual text or element on their page to edit.

checkpoints.title: Spot the Section
checkpoints.description: Locate the hero, feature cards, interactive canvas, and call-to-action on the target site

steps.title: Help the AI find the right section.
steps.instructions:
1.  Pick one section of the page.
2.  Tell the AI to make that section’s background pink. Describe which section it is so the AI could find it without seeing the page.

panels.text:
###Hero section 
The big opening area at the top that says what the site is

###Feature cards
Boxes that show what the site offers

###Interactive canvas
The area where visitors can play or create

###Call-to-action
The button that asks visitors to do something

questions.questionTitle: You open a website and see a big banner across the top with the site’s name and a short line about what it is. What is this section called?
A page has three boxes stacked in a column. Each box has a title and a short description of something the site offers. What are these boxes called?
A page has a small “Log in” link in the corner and a big colorful “Join now” button under the opening banner. Which one is the call-to-action?

steps.title: Project Level
steps.instructions:
**Do This**

1.  Look at your page and find the **hero section**, the **feature cards**, the **interactive canvas**, and the **call-to-action**.
2.  Pick two of them.
3.  Ask the AI to change each one, using its name in your prompt.
4.  Check the preview. Did each change land on the right block?

Missing a section? Say “I don’t have this one yet,” or ask the AI to add it.
steps.instructionsPrompt: Have the student find the hero section, feature cards, interactive canvas, and call-to-action on their page, pick two, and prompt the AI to change each one by naming the block. If a block is missing, have them say so or ask the AI to add it. Refer to the blocks as they actually appear on their page.

checkpoints.title: What’s It For?
checkpoints.description: Say what each block is for

steps.title: “Fix the complaint”
steps.instructions:
A visitor left three complaints about this page. For each one, find the section that should fix it and improve its words. Ask the AI or edit them yourself.

1.  “I can’t tell what this site is.”
2.  “I don’t know what they sell.”
3.  “I don’t know what to click.”

questions.questionTitle: A visitor lands on a bakery page and wonders, “What do they sell?” Which block answers that?

steps.title: Apply to Project
steps.instructions:
**Do This**

1.  Look at your page like a first-time visitor.
2.  Ask each question and see if your page answers it:

      - Hero section: What is this site?
      - Feature cards: What can I get here?
      - Interactive canvas: What can I try?
      - Call-to-action: What should I do next?
3.  Pick at least two blocks that don’t answer their question yet.
4.  Change them so they do. Ask the AI or edit them yourself.
5.  Look at your page again. Would a visitor get an answer now?

Missing a block? Add it so your page answers that question.
steps.instructionsPrompt: Have the student look at their page like a first-time visitor and check whether each block answers its question: hero section, what is this site; feature cards, what can I get here; interactive canvas, what can I try; call-to-action, what should I do next. Have them pick at least two blocks that don’t answer their question yet and change them, by prompting the AI or editing by hand, or add a missing block. Name the actual blocks and text on their page.

checkpoints.title: Speak Web Dev
checkpoints.description: Name the language a change needs (HTML, CSS, or JavaScript) and use it in a prompt

steps.title: Speak the language of web development

panels.text:
Speak the language of web development 

**HTML** says what’s on the page.

**CSS** says how it looks.

**JavaScript** says what it does.

steps.title: “Right file, right fix”
steps.instructions:
**Do This**

This page has three problems. Fix each one in the right file.

1.  The heading has a typo.
2.  The button is gray. Make it pink.
3.  The button’s message says “Error.” Change it to “Booked!”

Check the preview after each fix.

steps.title: Project
steps.instructions:
Pick one change you want on your page. Decide which language it needs: words (HTML), look (CSS), or action (JavaScript). Then ask the AI for the change using the name of the section and the language in your prompt.

Example: “Use CSS to make the call-to-action bigger and pink.”
steps.instructionsPrompt: Have the student pick one change for their page, decide which language it needs (words: HTML, look: CSS, action: JavaScript), and prompt the AI with the section’s name, a reason tied to that section’s purpose, and the language, as in: Use CSS to make the call-to-action bigger and pink. Name an actual section on their page.

checkpoints.title: Find the Clue
checkpoints.description: Point to the part of an error message or broken page that signals what's wrong

questions.questionTitle:
A page shows a broken-picture icon where a photo should be. The tutor shows this message:

skateboard-photo.jpeg 404 (Not Found)

You’re asking the AI for help. Which part is the most useful clue to give it?

panels.text:
###Clues to give the AI

- What you see: a broken-picture icon
- What the error says: the file name and “Not Found”

The more clues you give, the better the fix.

steps.title: Fix the missing photo
steps.instructions:
**Do This**

1.  Look at the preview. The photo is missing.
2.  Ask the AI for help. Tell it what’s wrong.
3.  Check the preview again. Is the photo there?

Here’s what the page is telling you: skateboard-photo.jpeg 404 (Not Found)
